मेखला मेखला, f. a girdle, belt, waist-belt,
(in one or two instances अस् or अम्, m. or n.); the
zone of a woman; the triple zone worn by the first
three classes, (according to Manu

. that of a
Brāhman ought to be of मुञ्ज, that of a Kṣatriya
of मूर्वा, that of the Vaiśya of शण or hemp);
the girth of a horse; a band or fillet; anything
girding or surrounding [cf. सागर-म्˚]; a sword-
belt, baldric; a sword-knot or string fastened to the
hilt; the place of the girdle, the hips; the cords or
lines drawn round an altar, or on the four sides of
the hole in which sacrificial fire is offered; the edge
or slope of a mountain [cf. नि-तम्ब]; Hemionitis
Cordifolia; N. of a place; of a woman; of the
Narmadā river, [cf. मेकला.]
—मेखल-कन्-
यका = मेकल-कन्यका, q. v.
—मेखला-पद,
अम्, n. the place of the girdle, the hips.
—मेखला-
बन्ध, अस्, m. investiture with the girdle; the
rites connected with such investiture.
—मेखला-वत्,
आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having a girdle or belt, wearing a
fillet.
—मेखला-विन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. wearing a
girdle.
—मेखली-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, -कर्तुम्,
to put on a girdle, to put on the sacrificial string.

मेखलाल, अस्, m. ‘having a girdle,’ epithet of
Śiva; (according to a Scholiast = मेखलयालङ्-
कृत.)
मेखलिक, अस्, आ, अम्, wearing a girdle.

मेखलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, wearing a girdle; (ई), m. an
epithet of Śiva; a Brāhmanical student or youth
who, previous to his marriage, wears a girdle suited
to his caste, Brahma-cārin.
